consensus_divergence.consensus_view: The market consensus has two legs and they point in opposite directions, which is itself the opportunity. On rates, consensus is firmly hawkish: almost 80% probability of a 25bp BoE rise on 5 November as at 30 September [28] and 39bp of cumulative tightening priced to 17 December [30], with MUFG holding its hold call 'with a little less conviction than implied by financial market pricing' and flagging that it would not have been surprised by a 5-4 vote on 17 September [30]. On the currency, vendor-composite forecasts sit near 1.3524 for Q3 2026 and 1.3638 for Q4 2026 - that is, roughly 2-3% ABOVE spot - and ING is the clearest dissenting voice, positive EUR/GBP on the argument that 'Bank of England expectations appear way too hawkish' [36].
consensus_divergence.our_view: We agree with the hawkish rate call and disagree with its currency implication. Our probability for the 5 November hike is 70%, below the market's 80% but still a base case, and we expect Bank Rate to reach 4.00% and stop. Where we part company with the bulls is on what that buys sterling: with 39bp already in the December curve, delivering one hike is worth close to nothing, and the energy shock that justifies the hike is simultaneously a terms-of-trade loss for a net energy importer running a 2.5%-of-GDP current account deficit. We expect GBP/USD at 1.3150 in one month, 1.3000 in three and 1.2850 in six, against forward outrights of 1.32340, 1.32383 and 1.32448.
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: Roughly 300-640 pips below the vendor composite at the three-to-six-month horizon: our 1.2850 six-month forecast against a composite near 1.3638 is a 788-pip (5.8%) divergence, and against the Q3 composite of 1.3524 it is 674 pips. Against forwards the gap is 84 pips at one month, 238 at three and 395 at six. On rates the divergence is narrow and in the dovish direction: we put the November hike at 70% against 80% priced, and expect a 4.00% terminal rate against the 4.14% the December curve implies - roughly 14bp.
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Three underweighted factors. First, the market is treating a 128.58% year-on-year rise in UK NBP gas [10] as an inflation event, which it prices through rates, rather than as a terms-of-trade event, which it has not priced through the currency - and for a net energy importer with declining North Sea output and limited storage the second channel is the larger one. Second, the market is pricing the Budget in volatility and skew but not in spot: one-month implied at 5.96% is 1.51 points above 20-day realised and the 25-delta risk reversal is 81bp bid for dollar calls [27], yet ING's point that sterling carries 'no fiscal risk premium' [36] stands against a 30-year gilt at 5.96%, a 10-year auction at the highest since 1999, and OBR headroom of GBP23.6bn against roughly GBP24bn of erosion [9][40]. Third, nothing we located prices the real-income arithmetic: a January Ofgem cap 16% higher [38] against real regular pay growth of +0.6% [4] turns UK real household income growth negative in the first quarter of 2027, which means the BoE hikes into a slowdown. The consensus error is sequencing - treating a rate rise that is already priced as a currency positive, and treating the energy shock that causes it as a separate, already-resolved story.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: Short GBP/USD or long EUR/GBP captures 382 pips (2.9%) on Cable and 327 pips (3.8%) on the cross at the six-month base case, with the favourable tail at 832 pips (6.3%) if the fiscal risk premium transmits fully. Against the vendor composite near 1.3638 the gap is 788 pips, which is the measure of the edge if the forecast distribution converges on us rather than the reverse.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: If consensus is right the loss is concentrated and fast rather than slow: a credible Budget on 28 October plus a hot 21 October CPI squeezes a -82,600 contract short [26] and costs 130 pips tactically and 368 pips (2.8%) to 1.3600 strategically, and because the squeeze would begin before the thesis's main catalysts land, the position is most vulnerable in exactly the first three weeks.

cleanest_bullish_expression.rationale: If the bullish case is right - the BoE goes to 4.25% and the Budget restores headroom - GBP/CAD is the cleanest way to own it. Sterling earns +150bp of policy carry widening to +175bp on our base case, because the Bank of Canada has no reason to move with CPI-trim at 1.9% and CPI-median at 2.0%, i.e. Canadian core is AT target [17]. The 10-year differential is +200bp on the gated store's monthly series, though that Canadian leg is four months stale and the magnitude is indicative only. Crucially the entry is tolerable: at the 74th range percentile GBP/CAD is the only positive-carry sterling cross not already at an extreme - GBP/CHF is at the 95th, GBP/SEK at the 97th with a 100th close percentile, and GBP/NZD at the 92nd. Carry-to-vol is 0.36 on 4.14% 60-day realised. The offset to be explicit about is that both currencies are oil-sensitive in opposite directions, so an Iran settlement that helps sterling through gas also hurts it through CAD's petro-currency channel.

cleanest_bearish_expression.rationale: The currency brief is explicit that when the thesis is about UK fundamentals rather than dollar dynamics, EUR/GBP is cleaner than Cable because it strips out the EUR/USD component - and this thesis is entirely about UK fundamentals. The evidence that the cross has not priced them is direct: EUR/GBP is 0.85727, DOWN 0.02% on the month and 1.69% over six, at only the 29th percentile of its one-year range, while Cable has already done 2.34% of the work. Sterling has therefore absorbed a 28bp rise in the 10-year gilt and a 1998-high 30-year without weakening at all against the currency that is 40% of its trade-weighted basket. The Budget-week option concentration is heavier here than in Cable - about 9% of nominal with roughly three-quarters bearish on sterling [27] - which says sophisticated money agrees on the vehicle. Two honest costs: the roll is against the position at roughly 134bp annualised (gated store, observed 25 September), about 8.9 pips a month against an ATR14 of 25 pips, so one average day costs three months of carry; and the ECB is also hiking, so if the BoE out-hikes it the rate leg works against the trade even as the fiscal leg works for it. That tension is why this is named the cleanest bearish expression AND a relative-value pair rather than a one-way bet.

relative_value_pairs.thesis: The single cleanest relative-value contrast in the set and one that works without any strong directional view on sterling. Norway is an energy EXPORTER running a 19.61%-of-GDP current account surplus with Norges Bank at 4.50% after a 25bp rise on 24 September; the UK is an energy IMPORTER running a 2.5%-of-GDP deficit with Bank Rate at 3.75%. The same gas and crude shock that worsens the UK terms of trade improves Norway's, and sterling already pays 75bp of negative carry. GBP/NOK is down 6.06% over a year at the 30th range percentile, so the trend is established and not extended.

Sterling pays the widest negative carry in the complex at -85bp against the highest policy rate in the set, after a unanimous RBA hike to 4.60% on 29 September with the Board noting 'some of the upside risks to inflation are materialising' and committing to go further if needed [34]. Australian trimmed-mean core at 3.6% is the highest in the eleven against UK core at 2.6% [16][3]. GBP/AUD at the 17th range percentile after an 8.00% annual fall is the one cross where the fundamentals and the trend already agree, which caps the upside but makes it the lowest-variance way to be short sterling.

relative_value_pairs.pair: Short GBP/SEK and GBP/CHF as carry-unwind candidates
relative_value_pairs.thesis: Not a sterling view but a positioning view. GBP/SEK at the 97th range percentile with a 100th CLOSE percentile and GBP/CHF at the 95th and 97th are the two most extended crosses in the complex, both held up by carry of +200bp and +375bp that the brief's own framework says stops working in risk-off and trend regimes. They are where a sterling carry unwind would be most violent, and therefore where a bearish sterling thesis has the best convexity if the regime turns - at the cost of paying the widest carry in the set to hold the position.

cross_horizon_consistency.summary: Aligned in stance and conviction - Bearish at conviction 2 on both horizons - but the strategic net score of -0.0915 is 57% more negative than the tactical -0.0583, and the two readings are driven by almost entirely different factors.
cross_horizon_consistency.divergence_explanation: Tactical bearishness comes from USD Liquidity (-0.0660), Event Risk (-0.0340) and Market Structure (-0.0280): a strong dollar, a dated fiscal binary and a bearish technical configuration, partly offset by a crowded short (+0.0600). Strategic bearishness comes from External Balance (-0.0992) and Fiscal Risk (-0.0490): a gas price up 128.58% year on year and a debt stock at 93.8% of GDP funded at 1999-high auction yields - against a Policy & Rates factor that FLIPS from Neutral to Bullish and contributes +0.1392, the largest positive in either table. So the tactical case is about the dollar and a date, and the strategic case is about the external account; three factors (Policy & Rates, Flows, USD Liquidity) change stance between the horizons, and in every case the direction of change is the opposite of what the overall score does. That is unusual and worth stating plainly: the thesis survives the horizon shift by substituting its reasons, not by extending them.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: 5 November 2026, the MPC decision and Monetary Policy Report. Before it, the rate factor is Neutral because almost 80% of a hike is priced and the asymmetry is adverse; after it, the rate factor is Bullish because Bank Rate at 4.00% sits against an SNB at zero, a Riksbank with cut risk and a Bank of Canada at target. The secondary inflection is late November, when Ofgem confirms the January cap and converts a forecast real-income shock into a dated one.
cross_horizon_consistency.catalyst_for_transition: The transition runs through two events eight days apart and then one a month later: the 28 October Budget and FOMC discharge the tactical drivers (the fiscal binary and the dollar's rate catalyst), the 5 November MPC converts the rate factor from priced-expectation to realised-level, and the late-November Ofgem announcement activates the strategic terms-of-trade driver. Positioning discharges across the same window: the -82,600 contract short is an event position that will not survive the event in either direction.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Express the tactical view in spot Cable and take it off into the Budget rather than holding through 5 November, because the window closes before the MPC and the position does not get paid for that event. Express the strategic view in EUR/GBP, which isolates the UK-specific thesis from a dollar that stops being a tailwind once the Fed's runoff decision and terminal rate are absorbed, and add on the post-MPC bounce toward 1.3250-1.3300 rather than chasing the first leg down.

forward_vs_spot.interpretation: The forward curve is almost flat - a 19.6bp annualised sterling premium across all tenors - because the GBP-USD policy differential is only -12.5bp on the effective rate. That means forwards offer essentially no cushion and no obstacle: a short sterling position neither pays nor costs anything material in carry, so the entire return is directional. The edge is therefore the full distance between the forward and our expected spot, 84 pips at one month rising to 395 at six, and because the forward curve is flat that edge does not decay with time - an unusual and favourable feature relative to, say, being short a high-carry currency. Two disclosures are material. The outrights are DERIVED, not quoted: no dealer forward points were sourceable in a free form, so they are extrapolated from the gated store's futures-implied roll premium of +19.6bp annualised observed 25 September over a 23.7-to-51.7-day window. A vendor 'market-implied' curve showing 1.3267 at one month, 1.3269 at three and 1.3273 at six against a 1.3255 spot on 1 October was read and rejected as the primary source, because a 12-pip one-month premium implies roughly 1.1% annualised against a 12.5bp differential and cannot be a clean forward.

key_catalysts.event: UK S&P Global / CIPS services and composite PMI, September final
key_catalysts.rationale: The flash readings showed the composite and services both at 51.7, down from 52.5 and below the 52.0 expected, while manufacturing improved to 52.0. A final services print below 51.0 would give the MPC doves a concrete growth argument eight days before the September CPI; above 52.0 would remove it. The effect is modest because the MPC has made clear that energy pass-through, not activity, is driving its reaction function.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced as a discrete event - PMI revisions rarely move more than 20 pips

key_catalysts.event: UK Halifax house price index and RICS house price balance, September
key_catalysts.rationale: The interest-sensitive housing channel is the clearest evidence of transmission: Halifax was -0.4% year on year, the ONS index +1.4% against 2.1% expected, Rightmove -0.8%, mortgage approvals 54.92k against 56.0 expected and the quoted mortgage rate 6.58%. The UK's short mortgage fixation periods mean rate rises reach households faster than in the US, so further deterioration here is the mechanism by which a November hike becomes a growth problem.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - housing data is treated as second-tier for sterling

key_catalysts.event: UK labour market release (ONS), covering June to August 2026
key_catalysts.rationale: The previous release showed unemployment at 4.9%, AWE regular pay decelerating to 3.5%, vacancies down to 702,000, payrolled employees -101,000 year on year and a claimant count rise of 27,800 against 8,300 expected. Regular pay at or above 4.0% would restore the second-round-effects case the BoE named as its key upside risk and make a November hike near-certain; a fall below 3.3% would undercut it. The ONS flags an LFS operational issue, so the wage data carry more weight than the unemployment rate.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - the hawkish 39bp December curve implicitly assumes pay growth does not fall further

key_catalysts.rationale: The last inflation print before both the Budget and the MPC, and the single most important scheduled data release in the window. August showed headline at 3.1% with core unchanged at 2.6% and services unchanged at 3.4%. Services at or above 3.6% makes the hike near-certain and is sterling-positive through the rate channel; at or below 3.2% unwinds much of the 39bp priced to December. Our expectation is 3.3-3.5%, which sustains the hike without adding to it.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - 39bp of cumulative tightening to December is priced, which assumes services inflation does not decelerate [30]

key_catalysts.event: UK Autumn Budget and OBR Economic and Fiscal Outlook
key_catalysts.rationale: The largest dated binary in G10 FX this month. The OBR's March headroom of GBP23.6bn (0.8% of GDP) has been eroded by roughly GBP24bn - about GBP10bn from rate and gilt assumptions, GBP3bn inflation, GBP4bn migration and GBP7bn unfunded policy - with 10-year gilt assumptions roughly 70bp higher than in March [40]. It is the first Budget of an administration whose Prime Minister moved the 30-year gilt 9bp with the word 'flexibility' [39], into a market where the 30-year is 5.96% and the 29 September 10-year auction cleared at the highest since 1999 [9]. The DMO's GBP252.1bn remit will be revised [8].
key_catalysts.priced_in: Priced in volatility and skew, NOT in spot: one-month implied 5.96% is 1.51 points above 20-day realised, the 25-delta risk reversal is 81bp for dollar calls, and 67% of Budget-week expiries are bearish on sterling against a 55% baseline [27] - while ING notes sterling carries 'no fiscal risk premium' [36]
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/GBP first (it isolates the UK story and carries the heavier bearish option concentration at about 9% of nominal), then GBP/USD, GBP/CHF

key_catalysts.rationale: Falls on the SAME DAY as the Budget, which is the compounding risk of the window. The Fed raised to 3.75-4.00% unanimously on 16 September and set IORB at 3.90% [31]; Williams has called one more increase before year-end 'a reasonable expectation' and Paulson said 'some modest further tightening may be warranted' [29], while August core PCE at +0.2% revived hopes of an October pause [25]. A hawkish hold with the dollar index above 120.33 compounds any UK-specific move; the sequencing matters because the Fed's catalyst lands eight days before the MPC's.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Largely - a hold with a retained hiking bias is the consensus, with one further rise to 4.00-4.25% by 9 December
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: GBP/USD above all others; neutral for EUR/GBP

key_catalysts.rationale: The ECB raised all three rates 25bp on 10 September to 2.50% deposit, 2.65% refi and 2.90% marginal lending, said inflation 'is set to remain well above target' and explicitly declined to pre-commit [35]. A hold keeps the GBP-EUR deposit differential at 125bp; a surprise hike narrows it to 100bp and is directly EUR/GBP-positive. With euro-area HICP at 3.2% and core at 2.4% [14] the meeting is live rather than mechanical.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Largely - a hold is consensus, but the September rise means the bar for another is lower than it was

key_catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting with Outlook Report
key_catalysts.rationale: The BoJ raised to around 1.25% on 18 September effective 24 September and said it 'will continue to raise the policy interest rate'. GBP/JPY has already fallen 3.84% on the month on that convergence while the VIX rose only 1.6 points, so the move is rate-driven. Each further step erodes sterling's second-widest carry, currently +250bp, and GBP/JPY has the highest realised volatility of any sterling cross at 8.30% over 60 days. Japanese headline CPI is 1.9% with core excluding fresh food at 1.7% [15], so the normalisation is being delivered against inflation below the UK's by 120bp.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - a hold at the Outlook Report meeting is consensus, with gradual normalisation toward 1.50-1.75% over the horizon

key_catalysts.event: Reserve Bank of Australia Monetary Policy Board decision
key_catalysts.rationale: The RBA raised to 4.60% unanimously on 29 September, noting 'some of the upside risks to inflation are materialising' and committing to raise 'further if needed' [34]. Australian headline CPI is 4.0% with trimmed-mean core at 3.6%, the highest in the set [16]. Sterling already pays 85bp of negative carry here and GBP/AUD is down 8.00% over a year; a further hike or hawkish hold extends the worst sterling cross.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - a hold is consensus with risk of one further rise to 4.85% by 9 February

key_catalysts.event: Bank of England MPC decision and Monetary Policy Report
key_catalysts.rationale: The pivotal event and the inflection between the two horizons. Almost 80% of a 25bp rise to 4.00% is priced [28] after the 6-3 September vote, with Lombardelli and Breeden the named swing votes [29]. Delivering it is close to a non-event for sterling; failing to deliver is a 30-40bp repricing against it. The underappreciated risk is the Report itself: because it conditions forecasts on market-implied rates, a CPI projection at or below target on a 39bp-hike curve would be an implicit statement that pricing is too hawkish.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Almost fully on the decision - about 80% probability priced, 39bp to December [28][30]. The Monetary Policy Report's conditioned projection is NOT priced at all

key_catalysts.rationale: Norges Bank raised to 4.50% on 24 September with Norwegian CPI at 3.3% and CPI-ATE at 3.0% [19]. Norway is the cleanest relative-value contrast to the UK in the set: an energy exporter with a 19.61%-of-GDP current account surplus against an energy importer with a 2.5% deficit, and sterling already pays 75bp of negative carry. The same gas shock that worsens UK terms of trade improves Norway's.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - a hold is consensus with one further rise possible by 17 December

key_catalysts.event: Ofgem announces the January 2027 energy price cap
key_catalysts.rationale: The mechanism behind the BoE's projection of CPI 'slightly over 4% in early 2027' [1]. The October-December cap is GBP1,723 after a 4% rise; Cornwall Insight forecasts January at GBP1,999, a 16% increase worth GBP276, and calls a rise 'all but certain' [38]. Against real regular pay growth of +0.6% [4] this turns UK real household income growth negative in the first quarter of 2027 - the arithmetic that makes the strategic case, and it is announced rather than forecast on this date.
key_catalysts.priced_in: NOT priced in the currency. Six-month at-the-money implied volatility of 6.724% is in contango beyond the October-November cluster, so the at-the-money surface charges no event premium for this date - although the quoted 25-delta risk reversal deepens to -1.073 volatility points at 195.7 days, so sterling DOWNSIDE at that horizon is partly paid for even though this specific date is not
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: GBP/USD, EUR/GBP - this is a UK-specific real-income event, so EUR/GBP is the cleaner vehicle

key_catalysts.rationale: The first inflation print after both the Budget and the MPC, and the first that can capture any Budget-related indirect tax changes. With the BoE forecasting CPI above 4% by early 2027 and services stuck at 3.4%, this release determines whether the December meeting is live. A services reading above 3.6% combined with a delivered November hike would put 4.25% into the curve.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced as a discrete event, but it conditions the 17 December meeting

key_catalysts.event: FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections
key_catalysts.rationale: The consensus terminal-rate meeting: one further 25bp rise to 4.00-4.25% is the central path, and the SEP will reveal whether the Committee sees more. A Fed that signals it is finished would cap the dollar index near 120 and remove the strategic USD headwind that has already been structurally reduced by the end of Treasury runoff [31]. A Fed that signals more extends the right-hand side of the dollar smile.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - one further rise is priced; the 2027 dots are not

key_catalysts.rationale: The second BoE decision in the window and the point at which the December curve's 39bp is settled [30]. If the MPC hiked in November, this meeting tests whether 4.25% enters the curve; if it did not, this is where the delayed hike would land. The ECB (with projections) and Norges Bank (with a Monetary Policy Report) decide on the same date, making it the densest central-bank day of the horizon.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - the 39bp priced to December implies more than one hike across the two meetings [30]

key_catalysts.event: Bank of England MPC decision and Monetary Policy Report (PROVISIONAL)
key_catalysts.rationale: Marked PROVISIONAL in the gated store's central-bank meetings file and presented as such rather than as a firm date. It is the first MPR after the January energy cap takes effect, so it carries the Committee's first full assessment of whether the 16% increase has produced second-round effects in wages and domestically-set prices - the risk the September statement named explicitly [1]. By then the real-income squeeze will be measurable rather than forecast.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - beyond the horizon of current OIS granularity and the date itself is provisional

That converts Policy & Rates from the largest tactical ambiguity into the largest tactical positive, and with the short at -82,600 contracts the move would be amplified by covering.

The brief's crisis correlation would then be active: gilts and sterling falling together rather than the higher yield supporting the currency.

A short that covers without sterling rallying means the position was not crowded enough to squeeze, which deletes the +0.0600 tactical contribution from Flows & Positioning and takes the net to roughly -0.118 - and strategically it means the next sterling decline has no positioning floor beneath it. Paradoxically, good news for the thesis.

invalidators.mechanism: This is the mechanical route out of the strategic thesis. Gas below 120p would cut the January Ofgem cap forecast well below GBP1,999, remove the real-income squeeze that turns UK household income growth negative in the first quarter of 2027, improve the terms of trade for a net energy importer, and lower the CPI path - taking External Balance from Bearish 62 to Neutral and removing -0.0992 of strategic weighted score, which alone flips the net positive.

invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Below 120 pence per therm for ten consecutive sessions, against 182.89p on 30 September [10]

invalidators.mechanism: This is the second-round-effects scenario the MPC named as its key upside risk. Genuine domestic wage-price pass-through, rather than imported energy, would force a two-hike path toward 4.25-4.50% and make sterling's carry advantage durable rather than cyclical - and because it would mean nominal incomes keeping pace with the energy cap, it would also remove the real-income argument behind the strategic bearish case.

It escalates rather than reverses the thesis, taking tactical conviction to 3, and it is the scenario in which short Cable outperforms long EUR/GBP.

It would validate the fiscal thesis directly, force index-constrained and mandate-constrained holders of the 25-30% foreign-held gilt stock to reassess, and move conviction to 4 immediately.

factors_changed.reason: The largest single change in the dossier and it is a two-step reversal. On 1 September the market had pushed BoE hike expectations out indefinitely - the previous dossier's own signpost recorded the probability of a hike by the 17 December meeting as 'effectively negligible'. The 17 September 6-3 vote with three members backing 4.00%, the projection of CPI 'slightly over 4% in early 2027', and Lombardelli's 24 September conditional-hawkish speech moved pricing to almost 80% for 5 November alone and 39bp to December. Tactically that repricing is now so complete that it removes the bearish case without creating a bullish one; strategically it means Bank Rate probably reaches 4.00% against an SNB at zero, a Riksbank with cut risk and a Bank of Canada at target, which widens the differentials sterling actually earns.

US high-yield spreads widened 42bp on the month to 302bp and the VIX rose 1.64 points to 16.07, while the US 10-year rose 51bp. The risk environment stopped being a sterling tailwind and became a duration shock in which the UK is the most exposed G10 sovereign - the brief's crisis correlation rather than its risk-positive correlation.

Stance unchanged, confidence raised 8 points. The legacy non-commercial net moved from -44,500 on the 28 August release to -82,600 at the 2026-09-22 report date, pushing through the currency brief's -80,000 stretched threshold for the first time, and leveraged funds cut from +42,877 to +13,239. The contrarian signal is now quantitatively confirmed rather than anticipated.

Tactical stance improved on two genuine positives: the Q2 current account came in at -GBP19.9bn against -GBP25.6bn expected, a GBP5.7bn beat with the trade deficit more than halving to GBP4.2bn, and Brent fell from the cache's USD114.89 to USD97.29 as Hormuz crude flows recovered to about 80% of pre-war levels. The strategic stance is essentially unchanged because NBP gas did NOT follow crude - it rose to 182.89p from 161.02p a month earlier, up 128.58% on the year.

The MPC has successfully moved market pricing from no hike to almost 80% for a hike without actually raising rates, and the unanimous decision to run gilt holdings to zero on a published multi-year schedule to 2034 replaced an annually-contested vote with a pre-committed path - a direct answer to the 2022 credibility episode. Confidence was set at 55 rather than higher because the Committee is simultaneously speaking with two voices and under-forecast August CPI by 30bp.

A pure calendar effect compounded by a fiscal one. On 1 September the Budget was eight weeks away and outside the tactical window; it is now 27 days away and inside it, and the OBR's March headroom of GBP23.6bn has in the interim been eroded by roughly GBP24bn of rate, inflation, migration and policy adjustments. The strategic confidence fell because the dominant event now resolves inside the tactical window, leaving a more diffuse residual.

Stance unchanged, confidence raised 14 and 4 points to the highest readings in the dossier. The 30-year gilt rose from 5.73-5.76% to 5.96%, the highest since 1998; the 29 September 10-year auction cleared at 5.383%, the highest since 1999; August borrowing overshot the OBR by GBP3.5bn with the financial year to date GBP8.1bn above profile; and August debt interest of GBP8.8bn was the highest August on record since 1997, including GBP2.1bn of RPI-driven index-linked uplift.

On 28 August spot was 1.35355, above the daily moving-average cluster. It is now 1.32318, below all three for the first time this quarter, pinned 4 pips under a five-touch resistance zone, with one-month implied volatility at 5.96% - the highest since 29 July - and a 25-delta risk reversal 81bp bid for dollar calls. The configuration moved from neutral to bearish without the underlying averages changing much.

Tactical confidence rose because the dollar index gained 1.88 points to 120.33 and the Fed hiked on 16 September, accounting for essentially all of Cable's 2.34% fall, with a quarter-end SOFR squeeze to 3.88%. The strategic stance improved to Neutral on a structural change: the 16 September implementation note directs the Desk to roll over ALL maturing Treasury principal at auction and recycle agency principal into bills, which ends the reserve drain and caps the structural USD funding premium.

Stances unchanged. Headline CPI rose from 2.9% to 3.1% but core held at 2.6% and services at 3.4%, so the underlying picture did not change; Q2 GDP beat at 0.5% quarterly. The strategic bearish case strengthened in substance rather than in score, because Cornwall Insight's January cap forecast of GBP1,999 (+16%) quantified the real-income squeeze that was previously only directional.

seasonality.pattern: Two documented patterns fall inside the horizons and one sits just beyond it. Year-end portfolio rebalancing in December affects all G10 currencies and, for sterling specifically, interacts with UK pension and insurance hedge-ratio resets - the LDI channel the currency brief identifies as the transmission mechanism of the 2022 gilt crisis - which matters more than usual this year with the asset-manager net short at -115,805 contracts. The January effect follows. The UK's own documented seasonal, April fiscal year-end repatriation and hedging, falls immediately AFTER the six-month strategic window closes at end-March 2027 and is therefore noted but not traded.
seasonality.relevance_window: December 2026 to January 2027 for year-end rebalancing and the January effect - inside the strategic horizon, outside the tactical one. The UK April fiscal year-end is at or just beyond the strategic boundary of end-March 2027.
seasonality.historical_magnitude: Not quantified in this run. No reliable free source for the historical magnitude of sterling's December or April seasonal effects was located, and the framework's instruction is not to fabricate seasonal patterns, so the direction is noted and the magnitude is recorded as unmeasured.
seasonality.current_alignment: Mildly reinforcing for the strategic bearish case. Year-end rebalancing lands in the same window as the January Ofgem cap, and the hedge-ratio channel is unusually loaded given a -115,805 contract asset-manager short and a 30-year gilt at 5.96% - the configuration in which hedging flows amplify rather than dampen a sterling move. This is a secondary consideration, not a driver of any stance.

assumptions: THE GATED CACHE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH wherever it holds a precise current figure: FX levels and all derived analytics (spot, moving averages, ATR, realised volatility, performance, 52-week percentiles, touch-counted support and resistance zones, futures roll premia), CFTC tranches, BIS REER, OECD macro vintages and scheduled central-bank decisions. Research supplies narrative, guidance, catalysts and citations around those numbers. The monthly snapshot used for the whole cycle is Data-Cache/2026-10/ and was not switched partway. Every GBP cross is read from its own file; none is synthesised from two USD legs.

POLICY RATES WERE TAKEN FROM THE EVENT STORE, NOT THE CBPOL SERIES, AND EACH WAS VERIFIED INDIVIDUALLY. Data-Cache/calendar/events/2026-09.csv was read directly and all ten decisions were located with their actual outcomes. THREE CACHED SERIES ARE STALE AND WERE OVERRIDDEN: CBPOL_AU shows 4.35% as of 2026-08-01 against the RBA's 4.60% of 29 September; CBPOL_NO shows 4.25% as of 2026-08-01 against Norges Bank's 4.50% of 24 September; CBPOL_JP shows 1.00% as of 2026-09-22 against the BoJ's 1.25% of 18 September. The other seven agree with the event store.

RATE CONVENTIONS ARE STATED EXPLICITLY. EUR is the DEPOSIT FACILITY RATE at 2.50%; the main refinancing rate of 2.65% and the marginal lending facility of 2.90% are given where relevant but no spread uses them. USD is shown as the 3.875% EFFECTIVE rate in every spread and table so the figures are comparable with the cache's own differentials; the 4.00% target-range upper bound is stated alongside throughout, and GBP's spread to the dollar is therefore -12.5bp on the effective rate and -25bp on the target upper. SGD has NO policy rate by design - MAS targets the S$NEER band - so its spread, rate and meeting fields are null or marked not comparable.

CPI FIGURES IN THE MACRO COMPARISON TABLE ARE THE LATEST PUBLISHED PRINTS, NOT UNIFORM CACHE VINTAGES, each dated in the core-measure field and cited. This is a deliberate departure: the cached OECD CPI vintages reach 2026-Q2 for AUS, CAN, GBR, NZL and USA but only 2025-Q4 for CHE, NOR, SWE and EA20, and Japan is absent entirely because the OECD prices flow returns 404 for Japan. Quoting 'the latest cached vintage' uniformly would have mixed a nine-month-old observation for Switzerland with a three-month-old one for the UK. GDP, unemployment and current-account figures remain cached point-in-time vintages with their periods labelled, EXCEPT the UK current account, where the ONS Q2 2026 print of -2.5% of GDP published 30 September supersedes the cached -2.84% vintage for 2026-Q1.

SCHEDULED CENTRAL-BANK DECISION DATES COME EXCLUSIVELY FROM Data-Cache/calendar/central-bank-meetings.json AND WERE NEVER WEB-SEARCHED. Two dates inside the strategic window are marked provisional in that file - the BoE's 4 February 2027 Monetary Policy Report and its 18 March 2027 decision - and are presented as PROVISIONAL rather than firm. SGD has no entry by design; the MAS semi-annual statement expected in the last week of October 2026 is given as 2026-10-W5 rather than as a specific date.

SOVEREIGN 10-YEAR YIELDS USED FOR GBP, THE US, GERMANY AND JAPAN ARE MARKET PRINTS, NOT THE CACHE'S MONTHLY SERIES. The cache's IRLTLT01 series are monthly and the GBP entry of 4.9886% as of 1 August 2026 is 43bp below the 5.42% market level; it is used for NO spread anywhere. The gilt curve of 2-year 4.75%, 10-year 5.42%, 20-year 5.91% and 30-year 5.96% is as at 30 September 2026. Three key spreads DO use the cache's monthly series - against Switzerland (0.47%, 1 August), Australia (5.015%, 1 August) and Canada (3.42%, 1 June) - and each is FLAGGED in place as indicative only.

THE PPP DEVIATION TABLE IS NOT A PURCHASING-POWER-PARITY CALCULATION. No PPP exchange-rate series exists in the cache and none was located in a current free form. The ten entries are a clearly labelled REER-RELATIVE PROXY computed as (GBP REER / peer REER - 1) on the 2026-08 BIS broad real basis, with implied fair values derived by applying that deviation to the cache's spot cross. Positive values mean sterling is rich against the peer.

GBP/USD FORWARD OUTRIGHTS ARE DERIVED, NOT QUOTED. No dealer forward points were located in a free source. The 1-month, 3-month and 6-month outrights of 1.32340, 1.32383 and 1.32448 are extrapolated from the cache's futures-implied annualised roll premium of +19.6bp observed 25 September over a 23.7-to-51.7-day window. A vendor 'market-implied' curve (1.3267 / 1.3269 / 1.3273 against a 1.3255 spot on 1 October) was read and REJECTED as primary because a 12-pip one-month premium implies roughly 1.1% annualised against a 12.5bp differential.

THE 3-MONTH CROSS-CURRENCY BASIS IS A DOCUMENTED GAP for GBP/USD, EUR/USD and JPY/USD. No free current quoted level resolved; the only ING research located on the subject dates from November 2022 and was discarded rather than presented as current. The nearest cache-grounded proxy is given instead and labelled as such: the GBP/USD futures roll premium of +19.6bp annualised against a -12.5bp spot policy differential leaves roughly 7bp of residual, consistent with the currency brief's description of a normally tight sterling basis. The gated store's own note on that field states that the interest differential and the cross-currency basis cannot be separated without an OIS curve and that the premium must not be reported as a policy differential; both caveats are respected - the 7bp is described as a combined residual, never as a quoted basis.

THREE PERCENTILES ARE ESTIMATES, NOT PUBLISHED RANKS: the one-year implied-volatility percentile of 70, the BIS REER historical percentile of 78 and the net-spec positioning percentile of 10. The cache holds no implied-volatility history, carries only the current REER period with a one-year change, and holds just 24 weekly COT tranches. Each is marked as an estimate where it appears.

THE TWO CFTC MEASURES FOR THE SAME TRANCHE DISAGREE AND BOTH ARE REPORTED. The legacy non-commercial net is 82,600 contracts short at the 2026-09-22 report date while the cache's Traders in Financial Futures breakdown shows leveraged funds 13,239 LONG against asset managers 115,805 short and dealers 108,142 long. The currency brief's -80,000 stretched threshold refers to the legacy measure, which is the one used for the contrarian call; the disaggregated breakdown is used for the composition analysis. The latest cached tranche is nine days before the valuation date and the next print lands 2026-10-02, after it.

GBP/USD IS THE ONLY GBP PAIR WITH A QUOTED IMPLIED-VOLATILITY SURFACE IN THE CACHE (CME at-the-money, observed 25 September: 6.236% at 41.7 days, 6.193% at 104.7 days, 6.724% at 195.7 days), supplemented by a research-sourced one-month level of 5.96% and a 25-delta risk reversal of 81bp for dollar calls. Implied vols for EUR/GBP, GBP/AUD, GBP/CAD, GBP/CHF, GBP/JPY and GBP/NZD in the cache are triangle-method ESTIMATES because no listed option exists on those crosses, and GBP/NOK, GBP/SEK and GBP/SGD have none at all. No cross-vol estimate is used as a quoted figure anywhere.

THE CACHE'S BRENT LEVEL IS STALE AND IS NOT PRESENTED AS CURRENT. The gated store carries Brent at USD114.89 as of 22 September 2026; the market traded USD102.59 on 30 September and USD97.29 on 1 October as Hormuz crude flows recovered. Both are reported, the divergence is flagged, and the directional conclusion rests on UK NBP gas at 182.89p a therm (+128.58% year on year), which did not follow crude lower and which the currency brief identifies as sterling's key terms-of-trade commodity.

SEVERAL FRAMEWORK-REQUIRED ITEMS ARE DOCUMENTED GAPS and are named rather than estimated: UK sovereign CDS at any tenor; quoted dealer forward points; the 3-month cross-currency basis; a UK terms-of-trade index (the NBP gas price and Brent are used as the directional inputs instead); the Bank of England sterling ERI as a cited series (a vendor level of 105.46 on 22 September was read but the BIS REER of 112.33 is used as the primary index and the substitution is disclosed); Fitch's current UK rating, which did not appear on the rating source read, so the brief's AA- is carried with that provenance stated; and Singapore's current account, carried at 16.7% of GDP as a vendor figure established earlier in this cycle and flagged as the least well-sourced number in the macro table. New Zealand's 2.7% sectoral-factor-model core is likewise flagged as best available.

SINGAPORE AND JAPAN ARE FULLY RESEARCH-SOURCED. Singapore is not an OECD member so no cached vintage exists: GDP +5.9% year on year and +1.4% quarter on quarter for 2026-Q2, unemployment 1.90% for 2026-Q2, headline CPI 2.3% and MAS core 2.2% for August 2026 are all research-sourced and cited. Japan CPI is absent from the cached OECD prices flow, which returns 404, so headline 1.9% and core excluding fresh food 1.7% are research-sourced.

PHASE 1 RESEARCH AND PHASE 6 VERIFICATION WERE BOTH PERFORMED DIRECTLY BY THIS RUN. Neither the deep-research skill nor any subagent or Task tool was available in this session, so the research fan-out and the adversarial fact-check were executed in-session with web search and fetch at equivalent depth - approximately 16 searches and 34 primary fetches - and the verification was run as a deliberately sceptical pass against the completed draft. The full cited research synthesis is checkpointed at logs/GBP_2026-10-01_research.md.

SCENARIO PROBABILITIES, TAIL-RISK PROBABILITIES AND INVALIDATOR PROBABILITIES ARE THE AUTHOR'S SUBJECTIVE ESTIMATES calibrated to the framework's 50/25/25 scenario convention, not market-implied figures. Where a market-implied probability exists it is stated as such - for example the almost 80% probability of a 5 November BoE hike and the 39bp of cumulative tightening priced to 17 December. Our own 70% probability for the November hike is explicitly below market pricing and is labelled as a divergence.

ONE SOURCE IS AN AGGREGATOR RATHER THAN A PRIMARY PUBLISHER and is flagged: the Ofgem October cap of GBP1,723 and Cornwall Insight's January 2027 forecast of GBP1,999 come from a cross-outlet aggregation. Ofgem's own January announcement is not due until late November 2026, so the GBP1,999 figure is a FORECAST and is never presented as a decision.

THE UK BALANCE-OF-PAYMENTS LEVEL IS LESS RELIABLE THAN ITS DIRECTION. The ONS reports revisions to the Q2 2026 release ranging from -0.5% to +1.7% of GDP on updated international trade surveys and improved measurement of global production arrangements. The headline deficit of -2.5% of GDP and the underlying -1.4% excluding precious metals are both reported, and the analysis rests on the composition and trend rather than on the precise level.

PHASE 6 ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION WAS RUN AGAINST THIS DOSSIER AND ITS RESULT HAS BEEN APPLIED. Every gated-store figure was re-derived directly from Data-Cache/derived/ rather than taken from the Phase 0 extract, and all of them reconciled exactly: GBP/USD spot 1.32318, the 50-, 100-, 200- and 200-week moving averages, 20- and 60-day realised volatility, ATR14, every performance figure, the 52-week range and close percentiles of 26 and 28, the quoted CME at-the-money volatility surface, the +19.6bp funding roll premium and the -0.125 policy differential. Policy rates were re-verified one by one against calendar/events/2026-09.csv. All 40 citations were fetched in this run, all resolved, and each supports the claim attached to it. TWO DEFECTS IN THE DRAFT WERE FOUND AND CORRECTED, both in Factor 9: first, the gated store DOES carry a quoted 25-delta risk reversal for GBP/USD (-0.914 volatility points at 41.7 days, -0.924 at 104.7, -1.073 at 195.7, observed 25 September, estimate=false) and the draft presented only a research-sourced 81bp while implying the cache held none - the cache value is now primary and the research print is shown as the later, narrower reading; second, the draft asserted that the volatility surface charges nothing for the strategic horizon, which is true of at-the-money volatility and FALSE of skew, since the quoted risk reversal deepens with tenor. Both corrections are marked inline as CORRECTED IN VERIFICATION, and Factor 9 confidence was LOWERED accordingly - tactical from 58 to 56 and strategic from 50 to 48 - which moved the tactical net score from -0.0583 after revision (from -0.0593 before). Neither stance, conviction nor net direction changed.

FIGURES THAT VERIFICATION COULD NOT INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRM are recorded here and read as best available, flagged, rather than as solid: the one-month implied volatility of 5.96% and the 81bp risk reversal of 28 September, which rest on a single secondary source [27] and are only partially corroborated by the cache's own 25 September surface at a different tenor; the 39bp of cumulative BoE tightening priced to December and the 'almost 80%' November hike probability, each single-sourced [30][28] though mutually consistent with the roughly 75% recorded four days earlier [29]; UBS's itemised decomposition of the OBR headroom erosion, reported at second hand [40]; the Ofgem GBP1,723 cap and Cornwall Insight's GBP1,999 January forecast, from a cross-outlet aggregator [38]; Fitch's UK rating, absent from the source read [12]; Singapore's current account of 16.7% of GDP, carried from this cycle without a fetch in this run; and New Zealand's 2.7% sectoral-factor-model core. The German Bund at 3.58% and the JGB at about 3.00% used in the key-spread table are this cycle's cross-currency prints rather than figures fetched in this run, and are flagged in place. One macro-table entry is outside both freshness windows and is flagged as such: New Zealand's 2026-Q2 CPI, released 20 July and 73 days old on the valuation date.
